PR3-F-01.hint: Each factor \((x-r)^m\) gives the zero \(x=r\), and the exponent \(m\) is its multiplicity. The \(y\)-intercept is \(f(0)\). For the ends of the graph, look at the degree and the sign of the leading coefficient.
slips: Reading a zero with the wrong sign. The factor \((x+1)\) gives \(x=-1\), not \(x=1\).
Using one exponent as the degree. The degree is the sum of all the exponents (times the leading factor).
Using only the sign of the leading coefficient for the ends. An even degree and an odd degree behave differently on the left.

PR3-A-01.hint: The multiplicity tells you what the graph does at a zero: an odd exponent means it crosses the \(x\)-axis, an even exponent means it touches and turns around. The ends come from the degree and the leading coefficient.
slips: Saying a zero of odd multiplicity greater than 1 only touches the axis. It still crosses; it just flattens there.
Forgetting that a factor of \(x\) means the graph passes through the origin, so the \(y\)-intercept is \((0,0)\).
